claim: Recent developments in detector hardware and image-processing software have revolutionized single particle cryo-electron microscopy (cryoEM) and led to a wave of near-atomic resolution (typically ∼3.3 Å) reconstructions.
source: Recent developments in detector hardware and image-processing software have revolutionized single particle cryo-electron microscopy (cryoEM) and led to a wave of near-atomic resolution (typically ∼3.3 Å) reconstructions.
evidence: This claim is supported by established knowledge in the field and is presented as a general statement about recent technological advances.

claim: Reaching resolutions higher than 3 Å is a prerequisite for structure-based drug design.
source: Reaching resolutions higher than 3 Å is a prerequisite for structure-based drug design and for cryoEM to become widely interesting to pharmaceutical industries.
evidence: This claim is supported by established scientific knowledge about the resolution requirements for drug design.

claim: The structure of the 700 kDa Thermoplasma acidophilum 20S proteasome (T20S) was determined at 2.8 Å resolution by single-particle cryoEM.
source: We report here the structure of the 700 kDa Thermoplasma acidophilum 20S proteasome (T20S), determined at 2.8 Å resolution by single-particle cryoEM.
evidence: This is the primary experimental finding of the manuscript, supported by the data presented throughout.

claim: The quality of the 2.8 Å reconstruction enables identifying the rotameric conformation adopted by some amino-acid side chains (rotamers).
source: The quality of the reconstruction enables identifying the rotameric conformation adopted by some amino-acid side chains (rotamers) and resolving ordered water molecules, in agreement with the expectations for crystal structures at similar resolutions.
evidence: This claim is supported by the experimental data shown in Figure 4 demonstrating rotamer identification.

claim: The 2.8 Å reconstruction resolves ordered water molecules.
source: The quality of the reconstruction enables identifying the rotameric conformation adopted by some amino-acid side chains (rotamers) and resolving ordered water molecules, in agreement with the expectations for crystal structures at similar resolutions.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 3 and 4, demonstrating resolved water molecules.

claim: Single particle cryoEM is capable of competing with X-ray crystallography for determination of protein structures of suitable quality for rational drug design.
source: The results described in this manuscript demonstrate that single particle cryoEM is capable of competing with X-ray crystallography for determination of protein structures of suitable quality for rational drug design.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the experimental results showing 2.8 Å resolution with features comparable to crystal structures.

claim: Direct electron detectors using CMOS technology have improved detective quantum efficiencies at all spatial frequencies compared to traditional CCDs or photographic films.
source: These cameras directly detect incoming electrons without the need for a scintillator converting the electrons into photons and are characterized by improved detective quantum efficiencies at all spatial frequencies compared to traditional charge-coupled device cameras (CCDs) or photographic films (Ruskin et al., 2013; McMullan et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior published work.

claim: The fast read-out rate of direct detectors allows for recording movies composed of multiple frames during typical image exposure times enabling correction of beam-induced sample motion and stage drift.
source: The fast read-out rate of these devices also allows for recording movies composed of multiple frames during typical image exposure times enabling correction of beam-induced sample motion and stage drift to reduce image blurring (Brilot et al., 2012; Shigematsu and Sigworth, 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior published work.

claim: Several algorithms have been developed for tracking beam-induced motion and stage drift in movies recorded with direct detectors.
source: Several algorithms have been developed for tracking beam-induced motion and stage drift in movies recorded with direct detectors (Campbell et al., 2012; Bai et al., 2013; Li et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior published work.

claim: Data processing strategies using motion correction have been used to produce high-resolution reconstructions of samples in the MDa mass range.
source: These data processing strategies have been used to produce a multitude of high-resolution reconstructions of samples in the MDa mass range (Amunts et al., 2014; Fernandez et al., 2014; Voorhees et al., 2014; Wong et al., 2014; Allegretti et al., 2014) as well as of protein complexes once considered too small for single-particle cryoEM (≤300 kDa) (Cao et al., 2013; Liao et al., 2013; Lu et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to multiple prior published works.

claim: Data processing strategies using motion correction have been used to produce high-resolution reconstructions of protein complexes ≤300 kDa, once considered too small for single-particle cryoEM.
source: These data processing strategies have been used to produce a multitude of high-resolution reconstructions of samples in the MDa mass range (Amunts et al., 2014; Fernandez et al., 2014; Voorhees et al., 2014; Wong et al., 2014; Allegretti et al., 2014) as well as of protein complexes once considered too small for single-particle cryoEM (≤300 kDa) (Cao et al., 2013; Liao et al., 2013; Lu et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior published work.

claim: CryoEM can compete with X-ray crystallography for determination of protein structures at near-atomic resolution.
source: This method can now compete with X-ray crystallography for determination of protein structures at near-atomic resolution while also offering the unique advantage of enabling the characterization of heterogeneous or flexible protein complexes (Scheres et al., 2007).
evidence: This claim is based on inference from recent achievements in the field and supported by citation.

claim: CryoEM offers the unique advantage of enabling the characterization of heterogeneous or flexible protein complexes.
source: This method can now compete with X-ray crystallography for determination of protein structures at near-atomic resolution while also offering the unique advantage of enabling the characterization of heterogeneous or flexible protein complexes (Scheres et al., 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work and established knowledge about cryoEM capabilities.

claim: High-resolution cryoEM can provide information about protein dynamics, which is key to understanding the functions of many macromolecular complexes.
source: High-resolution cryoEM can thus provide information about protein dynamics, which is key to understanding the functions of many macromolecular complexes.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the capabilities of cryoEM and established knowledge about the importance of dynamics.

claim: The T20S proteasome is a key component of cell metabolism carrying out degradation of ubiquitinylated polypeptides to regulate the concentration of specific proteins and eliminate misfolded products.
source: This enzyme is a key component of the cell metabolism carrying out degradation of ubiquitinylated polypeptides to regulate the concentration of specific proteins as well as eliminating misfolded products.
evidence: This claim is based on established knowledge about proteasome function.

claim: The T20S proteasome forms a 700 kDa complex comprising 14 α and 14 β subunits organized with D7 symmetry.
source: The T20S proteasome forms a 700 kDa complex comprising 14 α and 14 β subunits organized with D7 symmetry.
evidence: This claim is based on established knowledge about the T20S proteasome structure.

claim: Careful alignment of the microscope was performed before data collection to ensure Thon rings were visible up to ∼2.5 Å resolution in the power spectrum of micrographs collected over amorphous carbon.
source: Careful alignment of the microscope was performed before data collection to ensure Thon rings were visible up to ∼2.5 Å resolution in the power spectrum of micrographs collected over amorphous carbon using the same conditions as for data acquisition.
evidence: This describes the experimental procedure used in the study.

claim: Coma-free alignment was carried out to align the beam to the column optical axis with the assistance of a Zemlin tableau.
source: Prior to beginning data collection, coma-free alignment was carried out to align the beam to the column optical axis with the assistance of a Zemlin tableau (Glaeser et al., 2011).
evidence: This describes the experimental procedure used in the study, with citation support.

claim: Automated data collection was carried out using Leginon to control both the FEI Titan Krios microscope and the Gatan K2 Summit camera operated in 'super-resolution' mode.
source: Automated data collection was carried out using Leginon (Suloway et al., 2005) to control both the FEI Titan Krios microscope and the Gatan K2 Summit camera operated in 'super-resolution' mode.
evidence: This describes the experimental procedure used in the study, with citation support.

claim: 196 micrographs were selected based on a cross-correlation coefficient ≥ 80% at a resolution of 4 Å or better.
source: Only those micrographs showing a CC ≥ 80% at a resolution of 4 Å or better were retained for further processing. One of these micrographs and its corresponding power spectrum are shown in Figure 1. Using this selection criterion, 196 micrographs were selected, from which a total of 87,066 particles were automatically picked using FindEM (Roseman, 2004).
evidence: This describes the experimental data processing procedure.

claim: 87,066 particles were automatically picked from the selected micrographs using FindEM.
source: Using this selection criterion, 196 micrographs were selected, from which a total of 87,066 particles were automatically picked using FindEM (Roseman, 2004).
evidence: This describes the experimental data processing procedure with citation support.

claim: The movies have been deposited in the EMPIAR database with the accession number EMPIAR-10025.
source: These movies have been deposited in the EMPIAR database with the accession number EMPIAR-10025.

claim: 59,864 particles containing both top and side views were used for refinement and reconstruction after particle sorting and selection.
source: Particle images were sorted and selected based on mean and standard deviation pixel values within Appion (Lander et al., 2009) and using Xmipp cl2d reference-free alignment and clustering (Sorzano et al., 2010) to yield a stack of 59,864 particles containing both top and side views that were then used for refinement and reconstruction.
evidence: This describes the experimental data processing procedure with citation support.

claim: Thon rings are visible well beyond 4 Å−1 resolution in the power spectrum of the micrograph shown in Figure 1A.
source: Thon rings are visible well beyond 4 Å−1 resolution in the power spectrum of the micrograph shown in (A).
evidence: This claim is supported by the data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: The selected substack of T20S particles was refined using the gold standard procedure implemented in Relion.
source: The selected substack of T20S particles was refined starting from a low-pass filtered initial model to high resolution using the gold standard procedure implemented in Relion (Scheres and Chen, 2012; Scheres, 2012b; Bai et al., 2013).
evidence: This describes the experimental data processing procedure with citation support.

claim: Projection-matching refinement provided a reconstruction at 2.98 Å resolution with an estimated angular accuracy of 1.3° using all 38 movie frames and the full exposure of 53 e−/Å2.
source: This projection-matching refinement step provided a reconstruction at 2.98 Å resolution (estimated angular accuracy 1.3°) using all 38 movie frames and the full exposure of 53 e−/Å2.
evidence: This describes the experimental results from data processing.

claim: Previous measurements using catalase crystals have suggested that exposures as low as 11 e−/Å2 might be necessary to attain 3 Å maps.
source: Previous measurements using catalase crystals have suggested that exposures as low as 11 e−/Å2 might be necessary to attain 3 Å maps (Baker and Rubinstein, 2010; Baker et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior published work.

claim: The loss of signal due to radiation must be balanced against the need for sufficient contrast in the images to allow for accurate alignment of the individual particles.
source: However, the loss of signal due to radiation must be balanced against the need for sufficient contrast in the images to allow for accurate alignment of the individual particles.
evidence: This claim is based on established knowledge and inference about the trade-offs in cryoEM data collection.

claim: A T20S reconstruction at 2.98 Å resolution was obtained using the full exposure of 53 e−/Å2 and prior to weighting individual movie frames.
source: We emphasize that we were able to obtain a T20S reconstruction at 2.98 Å resolution using the full exposure of 53 e−/Å2 and prior to weighting individual movie frames.
evidence: This describes the experimental results from data processing.

claim: Similar results were obtained in determining the structure of an icosahedral virus to 3.7 Å resolution using an exposure of 38 e−/Å2 with a microscope operated at 200 kV.
source: We obtained similar results in determining the structure of an icosahedral virus to 3.7 Å resolution using an exposure of 38 e−/Å2 with a microscope operated at 200 kV (Campbell et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior published work by the authors.

claim: The results demonstrate that useful high-resolution information may survive much higher exposures than previously thought for single particle cryoEM.
source: These results contrast with previous measurements and demonstrate that useful high-resolution information may survive much higher exposures than previously thought for single particle cryoEM.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the experimental results showing high resolution at high exposure.

claim: The particle polishing procedure was used to account for individual beam-induced particle translations and to calculate a frequency-dependent weight for the contribution of individual movie frames to the reconstruction.
source: We subsequently used the particle polishing procedure implemented in version 1.3 of the Relion software to account for individual beam-induced particle translations and to calculate a frequency-dependent weight for the contribution of individual movie frames to the reconstruction (Scheres, 2014).

claim: The first frame of each movie featured a large movement in comparison with the following ones, interpreted as the initial settling of beam-induced motion during exposure.

claim: The particle polishing processing scheme improved the resolution of the reconstruction to 2.83 Å with an estimated angular accuracy of 1.0°.
source: This processing scheme improved the resolution of the reconstruction to 2.83 Å (estimated angular accuracy 1.0°), and this was supported by a significant enhancement of map quality.

claim: Plots of the relative B factor and Cf intersect, derived from the Guinier plots for each single frame reconstruction, along with the corresponding frequency-dependent weights are presented in Figure 2.
source: Plots of the relative B factor and Cf intersect, derived from the Guinier plots for each single frame reconstruction, along with the corresponding frequency-dependent weights are presented in Figure 2.

claim: Discarding particle images with the greatest angular uncertainty based on the height of the probability distributions at their maximum produced a map with a slightly improved resolution of 2.81 Å.
source: In a final round of refinement, we discarded particle images with the greatest angular uncertainty based on the height of the probability distributions at their maximum. An empirically determined cutoff of 0.07 was used, which gave a stack of 49,954 particle images (699,356 asymmetric units). Refinement of this smaller dataset under otherwise identical conditions produced a map with a slightly improved resolution of 2.81 Å (estimated angular accuracy 0.8°).
evidence: This describes the experimental results from data processing.

claim: An empirically determined cutoff of 0.07 for angular uncertainty gave a stack of 49,954 particle images (699,356 asymmetric units).
source: An empirically determined cutoff of 0.07 was used, which gave a stack of 49,954 particle images (699,356 asymmetric units).

source: This result suggests that analyzing the probability distributions over all orientations is a convenient way of discarding particles that are not contributing positively to the reconstruction (∼10,000 particles in this case).

claim: The gold standard refinement procedure prevents overfitting of noise.
